card: Updates sock_tests/send_and_receive to read socket data in a loop until the expected message length is reached, rather than expecting a single Recv call to return all data. This eliminates an invalid socket-chunking assumption that could cause intermittent test failures under partial reads. The issue was reproduced in test run #36751 using an artificial chunking patch and relates to test reliability issue #36726.
evidence: The PR author confirmed the failure mode with a reproducer patch that forces chunked socket sends: 'This was found -- and can be reproduced -- by using a reproducer patch, that forces all socket sends to use smaller chunking. For the run with the reproducer see #36751.'
Linked to issue #36726 regarding test errors caused by socket data chunking assumptions across the test suite.
problem: The unit test assumes that a 4-byte socket payload will always be delivered in a single `Recv()` call. While partial reads are improbable in standard CI loopback environments, TCP stream semantics do not guarantee atomic delivery, leaving the test vulnerable to intermittent flakiness under chunked transmission.

risk.why: A mistake would only cause sock_tests unit test failures or test hangs.

summary: Updates the `sock_tests/send_and_receive` unit test to read incoming socket data in a loop until the full expected message is received. This replaces a single `Recv()` call that assumed socket data would always arrive in one chunk.
